neighbours.label: a word that describes an object's geometric shape or posture (-shaped, triangle, upright)
fire: The island is roughly kite-shaped and covers about a hundred square miles.
The old church has an L-shaped floor plan with a short tower.
He wore a small beard trimmed into a neat triangle under his chin.
The new model has a more upright seating position than the old one.
The pool is oval in outline and lined with blue tiles.
The leaves are heart-shaped with finely toothed edges.
The garden is laid out as a long rectangle behind the house.
Each crystal forms a perfect cube when it cools slowly.
quiet: The island is mostly flat and covers about a hundred square miles.
The old church has a wooden floor and a short tower.
He wore a small beard that had turned grey under his chin.
The new model has more comfortable seats than the old one.
The pool is heated in winter and lined with blue tiles.
The leaves are dark green with finely toothed edges.
The garden is full of roses behind the house.
Each crystal turns cloudy when it cools slowly.

notes: Card top: diamond-shaped, triangle, upright, triangulo; weaker items (generations, since) do not fit.
